text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.65% today to $144.41, dropping $2.43 from Friday's close. The decline came as crude oil prices fell for a second consecutive day on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict, despite U.S. military strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island continuing. Lower oil prices directly pressure integrated oil producers like this one, whose earnings depend on the barrels they sell fetching higher prices.

The stock has lost ground over the past week despite trading as high as $154 just four days ago, suggesting the initial relief rally from geopolitical tensions has faded as markets price in the possibility of de-escalation. Political uncertainty around the midterm elections may also be weighing on energy stocks — a Democratic Congress is seen as potentially favoring renewable energy over traditional oil and gas investments.
